dn5:7.39: Since the ascetic Gotama has arrived at Khāṇumata and is staying at Ambalaṭṭhikā, the ascetic Gotama is our guest,
dn5:7.40: and should be honored and respected as such.
dn5:11.15: The king provided funding for those in the realm who worked in trade.
dn5:11.16: The king guaranteed food and wages for those in government service.
dn5:11.17: Then the people, occupied with their own work, did not harass the realm, and the king’s revenues were great.
dn5:11.18: The country was secured as a sanctuary, free of being harried and oppressed. The happy people, with joy in their hearts, dancing with children at their breast, dwelt as if their houses were wide open.
dn5:12.6: King Mahāvijita addressed the ministers and councillors of both town and country in the realm … the well-to-do brahmins of both town and country … and the well-off householders of both town and country:
dn5:12.7: ‘I wish to perform a great sacrifice. Please grant your approval, worthy sirs; it will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.’
dn5:12.8: ‘May the king perform a sacrifice! It is time for a sacrifice, Great King.’
dn5:15.4: while performing the great sacrifice, he might have certain regrets, thinking:
dn5:15.6: after the great sacrifice has been performed, he might have certain regrets, thinking:
dn5:17.15: Those who speak against the king in this way have no legitimacy.
dn5:17.16: For the king is indeed well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.
dn5:17.17: Let the king know this too as a reason to sacrifice, relinquish, rejoice, and gain confidence in his heart.
dn5:17.18: While the king is performing the great sacrifice, someone might say,
dn5:17.19: “King Mahāvijita performs a great sacrifice, but he is not attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty, with divine looks and lustre, remarkable to behold …
dn5:17.20: but he is not rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, lots of money and grain, and a full treasury and storehouses …
dn5:17.21: but he is not powerful, having an army of four divisions that is obedient and carries out instructions, so that he’d probably prevail over his enemies just with his reputation …
dn5:17.22: but he is not faithful, generous, a donor, his door always open, a well-spring of support, making merit with ascetics and brahmins, for paupers, vagrants, supplicants, and beggars …
dn5:17.23: but he is not very learned in diverse fields of learning …
dn5:17.24: but he does not understand the meaning of diverse statements, saying:
dn5:17.25: ‘This is what that statement means; that is what this statement means’ …
dn5:17.26: but he is not astute, competent, and intelligent, able to think issues through as they bear upon the past, future, and present. That’s the kind of great sacrifice that this king performs.”
dn5:17.32: But his high priest is not well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation;
dn5:17.33: That’s the kind of great sacrifice that this king performs.”
dn5:17.34: Those who speak against the king in this way have no legitimacy.
dn5:17.35: For the king’s high priest is indeed well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.
dn5:17.36: Let the king know this too as a reason to sacrifice, relinquish, rejoice, and gain confidence in his heart.
dn5:17.37: While the king is performing the great sacrifice, someone might say,
dn5:17.39: But his high priest does not recite and remember the hymns, and has not mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth; he does not know them word-by-word, nor their grammar, and he is not well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man …
dn5:17.40: but his high priest is not ethical, mature in ethical conduct …
dn5:17.41: but his high priest is not astute, competent, and intelligent, being the first or second to hold the sacrificial ladle. That’s the kind of great sacrifice that this king performs.”
